results.title: How I Use Claude Code to Ship Like a Team of Five
results.content:
Compare Claude Code to the alternatives:

1. Integrated development environments (IDEs) like Cursor, Windsurf, and Copilot require you to work within their special editor rather than any terminal you choose.
2. Agentic coding platforms like Devin and Codex want you to use their specific web interface, as opposed to an app that you download on your computer, and are more opinionated about autonomous coding.
3. AI chat interfaces like ChatGPT and Claude.ai are great for deep research and discussing code, but they’re conversationalists, not doers.

results.title: Anthropic's Claude Ship lets Claude approve routine pull requests - The New Stack
results.content:
To set all of this up, teams write those rules in .claude/approvals.yml, where they can also define their own classifiers in natural language. Anthropic recommends running the policy in observe-only mode first to see which PRs Claude would approve, before making its sign-off a required check.

PR Steward does its work before a PR gets to that point. It can act on feedback from people and other review tools, but it can’t approve or merge a PR. After each push, it comments on what it changed and how to undo it.

Admins can enable Claude Ship for a whole repository, and developers can also run `/ship` in Claude Code to push a change, open a PR, and work through feedback and failing checks. The command runs locally for up to seven days, so the session has to stay open and the computer awake. [...] Anthropic bills by the token. At Code Review’s launch in March, the company put the average cost at $15 to $25 per review (which isn’t exactly cheap, but cheaper than shipping broken code…).

Running `/ship` counts as regular Claude Code usage, and while Claude Approvals has no base charge of its own, classifiers consume billable tokens just like any other model use. Policies that call for Code Review trigger a paid review, even in observe-only mode.

There is a bit of a trial period, though. Eligible Enterprise customers have until Jan. 15, 2027, to claim “at least” $10,000 in Claude Ship credits, Anthropic says, but they have to use them within 30 days of claiming those credits. [...] ## How GitHub, Cursor, and CodeRabbit handle approvals

Unsurprisingly, other coding tool vendors are tackling the same bottleneck. GitHub, for example, introduced approvals for Copilot code review on Sept. 1 and made them generally available on Oct. 28. Admins can restrict which paths Copilot can approve.

Cursor’s PR Routing & Approval agent applies a team’s risk threshold and reads the APPROVAL\_POLICY.md file closest to the changed file. CodeRabbit lets teams set separate limits for merge risk and security risk in .coderabbit.yaml.

GitHub’s Max review level, now in public preview, also uses models from different providers and reconciles their findings. In Claude Ship, all three agents use Claude.

## How Anthropic uses Claude Ship

results.title: Claude Ship: Anthropic Now Lets Claude Approve Code, Too
results.content:
That makes sense, because Claude Code is Anthropic’s biggest revenue driver, as Trending Topics reported. With Claude Ship, Anthropic now covers not just writing code but the entire path to approval. Anthropic sees exactly this step as the bottleneck: When agents write most of the code, as is already the case on the Claude Code team according to Anthropic, everything after the pull request should move just as fast.

Anthropic is taking on a number of specialized competitors. GitHub also offers automated code reviews with Copilot, alongside start-ups such as CodeRabbit and Cursor with its review agent Bugbot.

## First Major Launch Since the I.P.O. [...] ## Claude Code Gets Its Own Ecosystem

Strategically, Claude Ship follows a familiar pattern. In September, Anthropic folded Cowork into the main Claude app and launched its own formats around it, such as Claude Docs and Claude Slides, followed in November by Claude Sheets and Claude Whiteboards, among others. What Docs, Slides and Sheets are for office work, Claude Ship is meant to be for Claude Code: an expansion of an existing product that ties users more closely to the platform. results.title: Anthropic launches Claude Ship, letting AI agents review, fix, and approve code changes | TechCrunch
results.content:
Anthropic is moving from having Claude write code to helping developers decide when that code is ready to ship. On Monday, the newly public AI company announced the launch of Claude Ship, a suite of AI agents for automating code reviews, fixes, and approvals of routine code changes.

The latter is the more interesting part of this new set of tools, as AI coding tools already offered code review features before now. What’s notable about Claude Ship is not just that it can review proposed code changes and identify and address problems, but that it also includes an agent that can approve code changes automatically based on policies set by a development team. [...] Because the offering is still in beta, Anthropic suggests running the approval functionality in observe-only mode first. Teams can also choose to start with just one repository and set monthly spending limits to have more control over the process.

Anthropic says teams will also still remain in control of where Claude Ship runs, which review settings to use (e.g., Quick, Standard, or Deep), and which changes should be escalated to a human for a decision.

Claude Ship is rolling out to Claude Team and Enterprise plans for repositories on GitHub. Code Review is generally available, while PR Steward and Claude Approvals are in beta.

When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission. This doesn’t affect our editorial independence. [...] Claude Ship is launching in beta, allowing early adopters to use it to review pull requests (PRs), and then decide what’s ready to merge.

The new offering consists of Code Review, which is already generally available, and two new agents now in beta: PR Steward and Claude Approvals. PR Steward focuses on addressing issues such as failing CI checks, merge conflicts, and feedback from Code Review. It also comments after every push on what it changed and how to roll it back, if needed.

Claude Approvals then applies an approval policy that the team writes as a file in the repository. This approval process can incorporate various signals, including Code Review findings or the company’s own classifiers, with policies written in natural language.
